companyIntro.name: Harbour Street Ventures
companyIntro.mission: Help small business owners and franchisees make money, not just stay busy.
companyIntro.culture: Know your numbers weekly. Cash is the scoreboard.

projectBackground.name: Neighbourhood Cafe Programme — Corner Cafe
projectBackground.context: The cafe is busy but the owner never has cash. You are asked to show where the money goes.

manager.name: Maya Chen
manager.note: Busy isn't profitable. Know your break-even and your best-margin products.

assignment.title: Make the cafe profitable
assignment.brief: Calculate break-even and profit, compare product margins in Excel, protect cash and write the owner's plan.

documents.name: Cost Data
documents.note: Fixed costs 6,000 a month; average price 12; variable cost 7.

documents.name: Menu
documents.note: Coffee, sandwich and cake prices and variable costs.

tasks.title: Break-Even Units
tasks.prompt: Fixed costs 6,000; price 12; variable cost 7. What is break-even (units)?
tasks.mistake: Ignoring variable cost makes break-even wrong.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Monthly Profit
tasks.prompt: At 1,500 units a month (price 12, variable 7, fixed 6,000). What is profit?
tasks.reasoning: Profit = unit margin x volume - fixed costs.
tasks.tip: Check at low, base and high volumes.
tasks.mistake: Using revenue as profit is the classic mistake.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Margin %
tasks.prompt: Price 12, variable cost 7. What is the unit margin (%)?
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Protecting Cash
options: Negotiate supplier terms and avoid overstocking
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Product Margins (Excel)
tasks.prompt: Unit margin in column D = B - C; margin % in column E = D / B x 100.
tasks.reasoning: Coffee has the best percentage; cake the best absolute margin.
tasks.mistake: Judging by sales volume alone hides low margin.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Owner's Plan
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence plan for the owner.
tasks.modelAnswer: You need 1,200 units a month to break even and sell about 1,500, which gives a 1,500 profit. Coffee earns a 71% margin and cake 60%, so we will train staff to offer a cake with every coffee. Sandwich margin is only 40%; I suggest raising the price by 0.50. Open a weekly cash forecast and pay suppliers on agreed terms to protect cash.
tasks.reasoning: A good plan uses the numbers to propose price, mix and cash actions.
tasks.mistake: Working harder without the numbers rarely fixes profit.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: Busy but Broke
caseStudy.background: A cafe was full every day but closed after a year. The owner never priced the sandwiches against ingredient cost.
questions: Why did a busy cafe fail?
caseStudy.solution: Harbour Street teaches unit costing and weekly cash checks.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Know the margin on every product.
